name: @attache/core
description: Parse, check and reason about Envoy proxy configuration. Route matching, reference checking and a config graph, with no Envoy and no network.
author: Louis Emmett
//publishConfig: Scoped packages are RESTRICTED by default, and restricted publishing needs a paid npm plan — so without this the first release fails with a 402 that no dry run catches, because --dry-run never makes the access check. Set here rather than passed as --access public on the command line so that publishing by hand from a laptop cannot differ from publishing from CI.
//files: src ships alongside dist. The declaration maps and source maps in dist point at ../src/*.ts, so without it they dangle and 'go to definition' lands nowhere. It is also the more useful half of this package to have on hand: the reasoning about Envoy's matching order lives in its comments, and a consumer who wants to know why a longer suffix wildcard beats a shorter one should be able to read that rather than infer it from minified output.
//engines: A floor, not a support statement: nothing here uses an API newer than this. CI builds and tests on 24.
//dependencies: One, and it earns its place. Every diagnostic this package produces has to point at a line, so parsing cannot go through JSON.parse or a YAML library that hands back plain objects — `yaml` keeps a CST with source ranges, and those ranges are what let the editor underline the field that is actually wrong rather than saying 'somewhere in your listener'.
